cards.title: In an emergency, nobody remembers anything
cards.body: Panic wipes out memory. Having key information written and ready means you can focus on getting help, not searching for numbers.

cards.title: Emergency numbers on the fridge
cards.body: 112 for emergencies, plus the family doctor, the nearest hospital and a neighbour you trust. Write them big and stick them somewhere obvious.

cards.title: Know the red flags
cards.body: Chest pain, sudden weakness on one side, confusion, trouble breathing or fainting means call 112 right away. Don't wait to see if it passes.

cards.title: One-page health summary per person
cards.body: Name, age, blood group, major conditions, allergies, current medicines and doses. Keep a copy in the file and a photo on your phone.

cards.title: Know where things are
cards.body: Medical file, insurance papers, ID, some cash. One known spot that every adult at home can find.

cards.title: Share it with your backup people
cards.body: Siblings, a neighbour, whoever can reach first. Send them the summary and update it when medicines change.

cards.title: Ten minutes today, calmer later
cards.body: Write it once, update it often. You'll hope you never need it, and be glad it's there if you do.

takeaway: Keep emergency numbers visible, know the red flags, and have a one-page health summary for each family member.
share: Make a one-page health summary for Mummy and Papa today. Numbers, allergies, medicines. Stick it up.
